stem: The chemical properties of oxides are related to the chemical bonding present in these compounds.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: A Period 3 oxide produces a solution with a $\text{pH}$ greater than 10 when it is added to water. State the formula of the oxide.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is added to an excess of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Write an equation to describe the reaction.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Table 2.1 shows the melting points of some oxides.

Table 2.1

| oxide | melting point/$^{\circ}\text{C}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{SO}_2$ | -73 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ | 0 |
| $\text{SO}_3$ | 17 |
| $\text{SiO}_2$ | 1610 |
| $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ | 1132 |
| $\text{MgO}$ | 2852 |
| $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ | 2072 |

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Identify the oxide from Table 2.1 that contains the element with the highest oxidation number.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
A student suggests the following hypothesis.

*The melting point of an ionically bonded oxide is only determined by the charge on the cation.*

Use Table 2.1 to deduce if this hypothesis is true or false or if there is not enough information to make a conclusion. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State why $\text{ZnO}$ is described as a Brønsted-Lowry base when it is added to $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: State the formula of the aluminium-containing species produced when $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ reacts with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: State the formula of the aluminium-containing salt produced when $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$.
